about: Suspension-bridge structure for the Delaware River bridges (pixelphilly.bridges.suspension_structure; scripts/05_build_scene.py with "bridge_structures": true): a raised deck in ~10 m steps with lane lines, tower crossbeams, two main cables, hangers and, on the Ben Franklin, the Warren stiffening truss that rises above the deck. Tower legs come from config/bridge_towers.json (pixelphilly.bridges.tower_legs) and are not repeated here. Method: the deck runs along the line between the two towers' centers (midpoints of the OSM leg pairs), from the back of one anchorage to the back of the other; anchorages sit one side span outside each tower. Deck heights are the median 2022 LiDAR first-return surface within 5 m of that line in 20 m bins, minus mean high water; where the LiDAR has no returns (the Walt Whitman's New Jersey end lies outside the City's coverage) a symmetric parabolic vertical curve through the published channel clearance stands in. Deck segments over water, and over land within the suspended spans (the side spans cross streets and terminals on piers), float on the deck thickness; past the anchorage front faces the deck stands on the ground (method.land_rule "anchorages"; "all_land" grounds every land segment). Cables run from each anchorage to the tower top, then along a parabola with the given mid-span sag; side spans use the main span's sag scaled by (side span / main span)^2, the shape of a cable under the same load per meter, which the LiDAR confirms on the Ben Franklin (about 10 m of side-span sag). Scene heights are meters above mean high water, the datum of the published tower heights. Every dimension is either sourced ({value, unit, source URL}) or an estimate ({value, estimate: true, reason}); 'measured' sources are this project's measurements of the cited dataset. Licenses: OpenStreetMap data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright); LiDAR: City of Philadelphia 2022 classified LiDAR via PASDA (https://www.pasda.psu.edu/uci/DataSummary.aspx?dataset=7154); tide datums: NOAA CO-OPS (public domain). Reference photos (public domain): Tichnor Brothers postcard (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Delaware_River_Bridge,_between_Philadelphia,_Pa._and_Camden,_N._J_(61748).jpg) and NARA 552709 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:WALT_WHITMAN_BRIDGE_CROSSES_THE_DELAWARE_RIVER_AT_SOUTH_PHILADELPHIA,_LEADS_TO_NEW_JERSEY_SUBURBS_-_NARA_-_552709.jpg).

mhw_navd88_m.note: NOAA station 8545240 Philadelphia, epoch 1983-2001: MHW 3.082 m minus NAVD88 2.110 m, both above station datum. The LiDAR is NAVD88; subtracting this puts it on the published heights' datum (above mean high water).

approach.about: Approach spans past the anchorages (pixelphilly.bridges.approach_decks, entries with "approach": true): the deck follows the entry's OSM deck ways outward in segment_m steps at the median 2022 LiDAR deck surface (within profile_half_width_m of the carriageways), until it is less than stop_above_ground_m above the local ground, the OSM bridge ways end, or they spread apart more than max_spread_m. Vertical frame: the main structure is in meters above mean high water (the river plane, y = 0 in the scene); on land the scene's y = 0 is the local ground and building heights are LiDAR surface minus LiDAR ground, so an approach's datum blends from MHW at the anchorage to the local LiDAR ground over datum_blend_m. Piers are not mapped in any source used here; their spacing and size are estimates.

pier_spacing_m.reason: Typical span of a steel or concrete girder approach; the actual pier positions under the Ben Franklin and Walt Whitman approaches were not measured.

pier_length_m.reason: Typical pier cap thickness; each pier spans the full deck width (an estimate too: real approach bents are often two or more columns).

deck_thickness_m.reason: Slab and girder depth for ~50 m approach spans; thinner than the suspended spans' stiffening truss.

stop_above_ground_m.reason: Below this the deck is at grade (an embankment or the street) and the aerial photo's road on the ground plane takes over.

datum_blend_m.reason: Distance over which the approach's height datum moves from mean high water (main structure) to the local LiDAR ground (buildings); avoids a step where approach meets anchorage. The two differ by ~1-3 m at the anchorages and ~10 m in Old City.

ground_radius_m.reason: Half side of the box around each segment where LiDAR ground returns are taken (the deck hides the ground directly under it).

max_spread_m.reason: Carriageways farther apart than this are separate ramps, not one deck; the approach stops there.

approach_fallback_grade.reason: Where the 2022 LiDAR ends on the New Jersey approach (~400 m past the anchorage), the deck keeps falling at the grade measured on the LiDAR before it: 33.7 m to 21.1 m NAVD88 over 400 m.

main_span_m.note: 1,750 ft. Not used for placement: the towers come from OSM (523.3 m apart).

clearance_m.note: 135 ft; also the Board of Engineers design report (archive.org metadata dates it 1921), https://archive.org/details/ReportToTheDelawareRiverBridgeJointCommission

cable_sag_m.note: 200 ft design sag. The 2022 LiDAR returns along both cables fit a parabola with 60.4 m sag (rms 0.3 m).

cable_diameter_m.note: 30 in. Real size; the scene uses cable_radius_m.

cable_radius_m.reason: Stylized: twice the real radius (0.38 m) so each cable is at least a pixel or two wide at map scale.

cable_anchor_above_deck_m.note: Measured: 2022 LiDAR anchorage top ~40 m NAVD88 beside a ~34.5 m road at the PA anchorage. The cables end on the anchorage top at its front face.

hanger_radius_m.reason: Stylized; real suspender ropes are a few centimeters thick and would not show.

tower_leg_spacing_m.note: 89 ft center to center. Not used for placement: cables and trusses follow the OSM leg centers (25.6 m apart); the LiDAR cables are ~27.4 m apart.

truss_depth_m.note: 28 ft Warren stiffening truss, top chord above the deck

truss_radius_m.reason: Stylized chord and diagonal thickness, enough to read at map scale.

deck_width_m.note: 128 ft overall; the LiDAR deck is ~40 m wide.

patco_tracks.note: One track outside each truss; also the design report.

patco_bed_width_m.reason: One standard-gauge track with clearance; the ~6 m outside each truss also holds a walkway (OSM ways 712972684, 712972687).

deck_thickness_m.reason: Road surface to the underside of the floor system: the 2022 LiDAR mid-span road (47.3 m NAVD88) minus the published 41.1 m clearance and MHW (0.97 m NAVD88).

vertical_curve_end_grade.reason: Grade at the anchorages of the fallback vertical curve, fitted to the 2022 LiDAR profile (46.4 m mid-span, 34.0 m at the PA anchorage, above MHW). Used only where the LiDAR has no returns.

anchorage_length_m.note: Measured along the bridge axis on the OSM bridge outline's wide end blocks (both ~47 m); the LiDAR block spans ~48 m.

anchorage_width_m.note: Measured across the OSM outline's end blocks

anchorage_rise_m.note: Measured: 2022 LiDAR, ~40 m NAVD88 block top vs ~34.5 m road (its decorative pylons, ~56 m NAVD88, are left out).

crossbeams_m.unit: m above MHW, [bottom, top] per strut
crossbeams_m.reason: Tichnor postcard (public domain): above the roadway a deep top strut, two intermediate struts and a strut just above the road, with X-bracing in the three panels between. Heights scaled from the far tower in the postcard (deck at 0, tower top at 1: struts at ~0.10-0.14, 0.38, 0.61, 0.88-0.95) onto the LiDAR deck at the tower (42 m) and the 116.4 m top; the top strut's top surface is measured (2022 LiDAR 113.1 m NAVD88, PA tower).

x_bracing.reason: Tichnor postcard: X-bracing between each pair of struts above the deck.

strut_thickness_m.note: Measured: the PA tower's top strut is 3.3-3.5 m wide along the bridge in the 2022 LiDAR.

lane_line_width_m.reason: Stylized: real lines are ~0.1-0.15 m; wider so they survive at map scale.

lane_line_height_m.reason: Raised just above the deck top so the lines draw over the asphalt.

dash_m.note: MUTCD 3A.06: broken lines are 10 ft segments with 30 ft gaps.

color.reason: 'Ben Franklin blue' (DRPA) has no published color code; same estimate as config/bridge_towers.json.

patco_rgb.reason: Ballast/track gray, a little warmer than the asphalt so the track beds read separately.

approach_fallback_grade.reason: The New Jersey approach lies outside the City's LiDAR; assumed symmetric with the PA approach, whose 2022 LiDAR deck falls from 40.4 to 16.9 m NAVD88 over 1,100 m.

main_span_m.note: 2,000 ft (PhillyRoads figures); also https://w.bridgemeister.com/bridge.php?bid=211. Not used for placement: the OSM towers are 610.6 m apart.

cable_sag_m.note: Measured: no published sag was found; the 2022 LiDAR caught both cables (one per half of the span along the OSM leg lines) and a parabola fit gives 60.5 m (rms 1.2 m), ~1/10 of the span.

cable_diameter_m.note: 23 1/8 in. Real size; the scene uses cable_radius_m.

cable_radius_m.reason: Stylized, same as the Ben Franklin, so the cables read at map scale.

cable_anchor_above_deck_m.note: Measured: in the 2022 LiDAR the PA cables reach deck level at the anchorage (~43 m NAVD88) and continue below the deck into it, so they end at the deck.

hanger_spacing_main_m.reason: No published panel length found; the Ben Franklin's 6.25 m.

hanger_spacing_side_m.reason: No published panel length found; same as the main span estimate.

hanger_radius_m.reason: Stylized, as on the Ben Franklin.

deck_width_m.note: Measured: the 2022 LiDAR deck is 28.7-29.6 m wide along the spans. DRPA gives 79 ft curb to curb; other sources 83 or 92 ft.

deck_thickness_m.reason: Road surface to the bottom of the stiffening truss, which hangs below the deck: the 2022 LiDAR mid-span road (52.8 m NAVD88) minus the published 45.7 m clearance and MHW (0.97 m NAVD88). No published truss depth was found.

vertical_curve_end_grade.reason: Fitted to the PA half of the 2022 LiDAR profile (51.8 m mid-span, ~40 m at the PA anchorage, above MHW), assuming a symmetric curve. Used for the New Jersey end, which lies outside the City's LiDAR.

crossbeams_m.unit: m above MHW, [bottom, top] per strut
crossbeams_m.reason: NARA 552709 (public domain), looking along the deck: one deep top strut with an arched underside between plain legs; nothing else is visible above the lane-control gantries. Top surface measured (2022 LiDAR 112.6 m NAVD88); depth ~9-13.5 m in the photo (scaled from the 30.3 m leg spacing), drawn flat at ~11 m.

x_bracing.reason: NARA 552709 shows no diagonal bracing between the legs.

strut_thickness_m.note: Measured: the top strut is ~5 m wide along the bridge in the 2022 LiDAR (both towers).

lane_line_width_m.reason: Stylized, as on the Ben Franklin.

lane_line_height_m.reason: Raised just above the deck top.

dash_m.note: MUTCD 3A.06: 10 ft segments, 30 ft gaps. NARA 552709 shows dashed lane lines.

color.reason: Painted green (CBS Philadelphia, PhillyYIMBY); no color code published. Same estimate as config/bridge_towers.json.
